questions.question: Sumit travels from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai at a speed of 40 km/hr in 33 minutes and he travels a distance from Navi Mumbai to Pune at a speed of 62 km/hr in 33 minutes. Find the average speed of the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total ~distanceover Total ~time ~taken

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 40 × (33/60) + 62 × (33/60)

Average speed = Total distance/T

questions.question: A man on his tour travels the first 180 km at 40 kmph and the next 120 km at 60 kmph. What is the average speed of the first 300 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed for first 180 km = 40 kmph

Speed for next 120 km = 60 kmph

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ Time = Distance/Speed

Average speed = Total travelled distance/Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Since, we have to calculate average speed for first 300 kms, then first 180 km will counted at 40 kmph speed and remaining 120 kms counted at 60 kmph.

Time taken for first 180 km = 180/40 = 4.5 hours

Time taken for next 120 km = 120/60 = 2 hours

Total time taken = (4.5 + 2) hours = 6.5 hours

Total distance = 300 km

Average speed = 300/6.5 ≈ 
46.15 kmph

**Thus, the average speed for 300 km is 46.15 kmph.**

questions.question: A metro train runs at the speed of 40 km/h from station A to station B covering a distance of 30 km. It stops at 5 stations in between, for 5 minutes at each station. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the train from A to B?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of the metro train from A to B = 40 km/hour

Distance between A and B = 30 km

It stops at 5 stations for 5 minutes each.

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Average Speed = Total Distance/Total Time

Calculation:

According to question,

Time = Distance/ Speed = 30/40 = 3/4 h

⇒ Total time of journey

= 3/4 + 5 minutes × 5

= 3/4 + ( 5 × 5/60)

= 3/4 + 5/12

= 14/12 

= 7/6 hours 

Average Speed = Total Distance/Total Time

= 30/(7/6)

= 180/7

= 25.7 km/h

∴ The Required average speed is 25.7 km/h.

questions.question: Raman travel a distance of 120 km with speed of 60 km/hr and 200 km with 100 km/hr. Find the average speed of Raman.
questions.solution:
Given:

Raman travels a distance of 120 km with a speed of 60 km/hr and 200 km with 100 km/hr.

**Formula used:**

(1.) Average speed = frac{ {Total distance}}{ {Total time}}

(2.) Time = frac{ {Distance}}{ {Speed}}

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Time taken to travel 120 km with speed of 60 km/hr = (120)/(60) = 2 hours

Time taken to travel 200 km with speed of 100 km/hr = (200)/(100) = 2 hours

Total distance = 120 + 200 = 320 km

Total time = 2 + 2 = 4 hours

Average speed = (320)/(4) = 80 km/hr

**Therefore, '80 km/hr' is the required answer.**

questions.question: A car travels from P to Q with a speed of 45 km/h and from Q to R with a speed of 65 km/h. If the distance from P to Q is 60 km and the distance from Q to R is 100 km, then what is the average speed of the car during the whole journey (corrected to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance(P-Q) = 60km

Distance(Q-R) = 100km

Speed(P-Q) =45km/h

Speed(Q-R) = 65km/h

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time 

Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time taken

**Solution:**

Total distance = 60 + 100 = 160

Time from P to Q = 60/45 = 1.33 hours

Time from Q to R = 100/65 = 1.538 hours

Total time = 1.33 + 1.538 = 2.868 hours

**Average speed = 160/2.868 = 55.79km/h**

questions.question: A man travels for 4 hours at a speed of 75 km/h, for next 6 hours at a speed of 65.5 km/h and for next 2 hours at a speed of 54 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = (4 × 75) + (6 × 65.5) + (2 × 54) = 300 + 393 + 108 = 801 km

Total Time = 4 + 6 + 2 = 12 hours

Average Speed = 801 ÷ 12 = 267 ÷ 4 = 66 ³/₄ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 66 ³/₄ km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time for part 1 = 4 hours, Speed for part 1 = 75 km/h

Time for part 2 = 6 hours, Speed for part 2 = 65.5 km/h

Time for part 3 = 2 hours, Speed for part 3 = 54 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/415369841e3a61930191dc7f0cfe28c25e170c6bcf900927e5eb59d56a68b96d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 6 + 2 = 12 hours

⇒ Distance for part 1 = 4 × 75 = 300 km

⇒ Distance for part 2 = 6 × 65.5 = 393 km

⇒ Distance for part 3 = 2 × 54 = 108 km

⇒ Total Distance = 300 + 393 + 108 = 801 km

⇒ Average Speed = 801 ÷ 12

⇒ Average Speed = 267 ÷ 4 = 66 ³/₄ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 66 ³/₄ km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person travels equal distances at speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
</p

questions.question: The distance between stations A and B is 778 kilometres. A train travels from station A to station B at a uniform speed of 84 km/h and then returns to station A at a uniform speed of 56 km/h. What is the train's average speed (in km/h) throughout the journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance is constant for both parts of a journey, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y)

⇒ Forward speed (x) = 84 km/h, Return speed (y) = 56 km/h

⇒ Average speed = (2 × 84 × 56) ÷ (84 + 56)

⇒ Average speed = (2 × 84 × 56) ÷ 140

⇒ Average speed = 9408 ÷ 140 = 67.2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 67.2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

•

 Return Speed = 56 km/h

**Given:**

⇒ Distance between stations A and B = 778 km

⇒ Forward speed (v₁) = 84 km/h

⇒ Return speed (v₂) = 56 km/h

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance for the round trip = 778 + 778 = 1556 km

⇒ Time taken from A to B = 778 ÷ 84 hours

⇒ Time taken from B to A = 778 ÷ 56 hours

⇒ Total Time = (778 ÷ 84) + (778 ÷ 56)

⇒ Taking 778 common, Total Time = 778 × (1/84 + 1/56)

⇒ LCM of 84 and 56 is 168. Therefore, 1/84 + 1/56 = (2 + 3) ÷ 168 = 5 ÷ 168

⇒ Total Time = (778 × 5) ÷ 168 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 1556 ÷ [(778 × 5) ÷ 168]

⇒ Average Speed = (1556 × 168) ÷ (778 × 5)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 168) ÷ 5 = 336 ÷ 5 = 67.2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 67.2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

When different distances are covered at varying speeds, the direct formula cannot be used. Always apply the base formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a vehicle covers three equal parts of a journey at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the overall average speed is calculated as: 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other (opposite directions), their Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

questions.question: A person covers a certain distance at the speed of 60 kmph and returns to the starting point at a speed of 40 kmph. Find the average speed (in km/hour) of the person for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person covers a certain distance at the speed of 60 kmph

Returns to the starting point at a speed of 40 kmph

**Formula used:**

Average speed = dfrac{2 × s1 × s2}{s1 + s2} (where s1 and s2 are the respective speeds)

**Calculations:**

Average speed = dfrac{2 × 40 × 60}{60 + 40}

=> dfrac{2 × 60 × 40}{100}

=> 2 × 6 × 4

=> 48

**∴ The answer is 48 kmph.**
